speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative check-up. I see you are experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if they occur on both sides?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain specifically occurs when you eat, which suggests referred otalgia; is the pain sharp and stabbing, and does it radiate to your jaw or teeth? REQUEST TEST: CT_Temporal_Bone to evaluate for graft displacement, ossicular chain issues, or cholesteatoma recurrence.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigeminal Neuralgia (Secondary to post-tympanoplasty scarring or neuroma). The combination of shooting pain triggered by chewing (V2/V3 distribution) and mechanical discomfort with earrings (V3 involvement) strongly points to cranial nerve irritation rather than middle ear pathology. The normal CT and hearing improvement rule out graft failure or cholesteatoma.
